cells.tense: You are here, with the pen in hand, seeing what matters without needing the argument.
cells.act: set one rule that makes the rest easier
cells.ask: Look at the one mess you keep stepping around — the papers, the messages, the half-made plan. Set a single rule for it. Just one, and small enough to keep.
cells.core:
Something you've been circling comes down clean, and you don't argue with it. In a room, you catch what the room is about before anyone says it — and lately the catch has been good enough that you skip the argument and go straight to the thing. That's the working version, and it is working here.

The next thing this balance is free to feed is structure: giving the cleared ground a shape the rest can stand on. One rule that makes the other rules unnecessary. Not a system, just a single line you'd actually keep. What you see plainly already suggests which line it is, so pick it and put it where you'll see it. Structure isn't the opposite of clear sight. It's what keeps the sight from washing out when the week gets loud and the requests stack up.
cells.sheetLine: You see what matters. Give it one line to stand on.
cells.verb: knowing what matters before you can say why
cells.place: the moment a structure that couldn't hold finally comes down

cells.tense: You will have read everything, and you will still be braced for a clearing no amount of reading can write.
cells.act: pick the one you would be sorriest to lose
cells.ask: Ask yourself what you'd keep if the whole pile went, and answer honestly once. No ranking, no defense — just the plain want, held for a minute with nothing done about it.
cells.core:
When the reading runs past the clearing, the veil gets thick enough to lean on. One more source, one more angle, one more day with the decision held open — and the pile grows past what any of it was ever for. Nothing has come down. You're braced for a landing you can't predict.

What pulls you out isn't more analysis. It's wanting something clearly enough to turn toward it. Pick the one you would miss most if the whole pile went — not the safest, not the most defensible, the one that would actually hurt. Let yourself want it, plainly, to yourself, for one minute. The pile shows its real size next to that. You'll know what to do with it then, and you'll do less.

cells.tense: You have been standing at a door that is already behind you, asking others to confirm what you noticed.
cells.act: move through the fog without demanding the map
cells.ask: Take the next small thing on your list and do it without checking with anyone first. One step, unconfirmed, taken into whatever is unclear.
cells.core:
The clearing already happened, and you're standing past it, still checking whether the ground is real. You keep running your read past someone else — a friend, a feed, a person who'd know — and the checking has become the habit. Nothing has arrived where you are. You're at a door that closed behind you.

What moves is not more certainty. A little light, enough for one step. Take the next small thing and do it without checking. Not because you're sure — because the step is the only place the next patch of ground appears. Walk into what you haven't figured out, and the ground reveals itself in patches, at the pace walking sets. That is how the path was always going to show itself.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you. Take one step in the light you have.

cells.tense: You are already writing in this room with the pen down, and the calls keep surprising you afterward.
cells.act: put it in proportion, not in punishment
cells.ask: Name one place where the balance has tipped — a favour, a debt, a thing you're carrying. Adjust the share until it's fair, once, then stop. No speech, no accounting.
cells.core:
The perceptions that land keep being right, and the surprise is that you didn't know you'd made the call. You describe the choice as a coin flip, and it turns out you'd already seen the whole coin. Among people, that shows up as a room that goes quiet when you walk in — not authority, just things in proportion around you.

One exchange has slipped, though, and you'd say it's fine. Find it: something owed, something carried too long, a share that tilted. Give back what's owed, or take what's yours — once, plainly, no speech. The fairness you keep is not a calculation you run; it's what's left when the account is settled. Settle one, and the call stops arriving as a surprise.
cells.sheetLine: You keep making the right call and calling it luck.

attempts.check: The record says Wisdom at Breakthrough is 'knowing what to attend to' meeting 'sudden clearing of false structure' — it does not say the person has been confused for years, lost anyone, or that any particular structure in their life is false. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not in a sudden clearing, I'm just tired,' or 'my confusion isn't about perception, it's about a real decision.' The asks survive being wrong because each is a small, done-once act from the medicine's own list — a date, a picture, a trade, a shape — useful even if the read is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that implies I know which structure is collapsing; cut it. Write the seat as weather that arrives, not as a verdict on their life.
